prompt.context: Your client, Maxicure, manufactures and sells an over-the-counter cough and cold medicine. Their sole plant in Kentucky is aging, and its increasing maintenance costs are leading to low margins on their products.
prompt.question: How would you advise Maxicure proceed to solve this problem?

clarifying_info.a: There are 2-3 larger players in this over-the-counter business who have distribution across the country. Maxicure is one of them.

clarifying_info.q: Where does Maxicure sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: Maxicure sells all of its products in the US.
The objective is to reduce production costs while maintaining product quality. Cost, quality, and brand image all matter to customers.

framework: Identify options: Refurbish existing plant, Rebuild on same site, Rebuild at new location, Outsource manufacturing

Evaluate each option across: Investment cost, New per-unit production cost, Financial and non-financial benefits, Effect on product quality, Opportunity to improve technology and capacity, Proximity to distribution centers

questions.prompt: What options does Maxicure have for tackling this problem, and what factors would you consider in deciding which option to choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure a MECE set of options (refurbish, rebuild same site, rebuild new location, outsource) and evaluate them across both financial dimensions (investment cost, per-unit cost) and operational/strategic dimensions (quality impact, tech upgrade opportunity, proximity to distribution). Strong answers will explicitly weigh cost vs. quality vs. flexibility trade-offs.

questions.prompt: Maxicure has narrowed down its decision to 2 options: (1) build a new facility next to the old plant, or (2) outsource the manufacturing to a competitor. With the information below, how many bottles of medicine would Maxicure need to sell for the in-house option to be more profitable than the outsourcing option? Data: Selling price per bottle: $4.50. In-house: Initial investment $50M, total cost per bottle $2.00. Outsource: total cost per bottle $2.25 for first 20M bottles (regardless of total order size); $2.50 per bottle for bottles after the first 20M.
questions.guidance: Candidate must set up a break-even equation comparing cumulative profits under each option. After solving, interviewer should push candidate to select an option and provide reasons why. Key insight: outsourcing becomes less attractive at high volumes because the per-unit cost rises above $2.25 after 20M units, while in-house has a fixed upfront cost but lower and constant per-unit cost.

math.setup: Find x (total bottles) where in-house cumulative profit equals outsource cumulative profit. In-house margin per bottle = $4.50 - $2.00 = $2.50. Outsource margin per bottle: $4.50 - $2.25 = $2.25 for first 20M bottles; $4.50 - $2.50 = $2.00 for bottles beyond 20M. In-house profit = 2.5x - 50M. Outsource profit (assuming x > 20M) = (2.25 * 20M) + (2.00 * (x - 20M)).
math.answer: 110 million bottles. If Maxicure expects to sell more than 110M bottles, in-house manufacturing is more profitable; below 110M, outsourcing is more profitable.

questions.prompt: Maxicure has decided to build a new production facility in Indiana instead of Kentucky to be closer to a major distribution center. How should it convince the governor of Indiana to offer Maxicure the necessary tax breaks?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm arguments from the state's and governor's perspective — economic, political, and community benefits. Strong answers cover multiple stakeholder angles.

brainstorming.prompt: How should Maxicure convince the governor of Indiana to offer tax breaks for its new facility?

categories.name: Economic benefits for the state
ideas: Increased tax collection from employee income taxes and business activity
Stimulates local economy through supply chain and services spending
Attracts other manufacturers to the state signaling pro-business environment

categories.name: Employment and social benefits
ideas: Community-building initiatives such as building schools and parks

categories.name: Political benefits for the governor
ideas: Good press and public relations boost for the governor
Demonstrates ability to attract major businesses
Strengthens re-election platform with tangible economic achievements

recommendation: Maxicure should build a new production facility in Indiana near a major distribution center, as it addresses the root cause of rising costs from the aging Kentucky plant while enabling operational improvements
The new facility allows Maxicure to upgrade technology, reduce per-unit production costs to $2.00, and improve proximity to distribution, supporting long-term margin improvement
risks: Execution risk: construction delays or cost overruns on the $50M investment
Break-even requires selling more than 110M bottles, so demand forecasting is critical
Transition risk: maintaining product quality and supply continuity during the move from Kentucky to Indiana
Regulatory and community relations risk in Kentucky if the plant closure leads to job losses
next_steps: Conduct detailed demand forecast to validate that expected sales volumes exceed the 110M break-even threshold
Negotiate tax break terms with the Indiana governor using economic, employment, and community benefit arguments
Develop a phased transition plan to maintain supply continuity and manage workforce impacts in Kentucky
Finalize site selection, engineering plans, and contractor bids for the Indiana facility
